definition: The quality of being proper and socially approved of.

collocations.example: The old hotel still keeps an air of respectability despite its age.
He hid his crimes behind a cloak of respectability for years.

definition: To say something again in a different or clearer way.

collocations.example: Please restate your position so the whole committee can understand it.
The teacher asked us to restate the problem in simpler words.

definition: Unwillingness to talk about your thoughts or feelings.

collocations.example: Her natural reticence made it hard to know her true feelings.
He finally broke his reticence and spoke about the accident.

definition: Severe punishment given as deserved payback for a wrong.

collocations.example: Many witnesses stayed silent for fear of retribution from the gang.
The victims' families wanted to seek retribution through the courts.

definition: To change and improve the form or appearance of something.

collocations.example: The company plans to revamp the whole booking system next year.
They hired a designer to revamp the brand's tired image.

definition: A small handgun with a rotating cylinder that holds bullets.

collocations.example: The officer found a loaded revolver hidden inside the drawer.
He slowly pointed the revolver at the locked steel door.

definition: A large, heavy animal with thick skin and horns on its nose.

collocations.example: The black rhino is still hunted illegally for its horn.
A baby rhino stayed close to its mother all day.

definition: The hard or tough outer skin of certain fruits or cheese.

collocations.example: She grated some lemon rind into the cake batter.
Cut away the thick cheese rind before slicing it.

definition: A flat surface of ice or a building used for skating.

collocations.example: We spent the afternoon at the new ice rink downtown.
The skating rink opens to the public every winter evening.

definition: To play in a lively, energetic, and happy way.

collocations.example: The children love to romp around in the fresh snow.
The puppies romped happily in the garden all morning.

definition: A person who has just started a job and has little experience.

collocations.example: Forgetting to save the file was a classic rookie mistake.
The manager asked me to train the new rookie.

definition: A list showing people's names and when they are due to work.

collocations.example: The duty roster shows who works each weekend this month.
Please check the staff roster before you book your holiday.

definition: Moving in a circle around a central point.

collocations.example: The old clock uses a simple rotary motion to turn.
A rotary engine usually has fewer moving parts than a piston one.

definition: Not direct; going the long way instead of the short way.

collocations.example: We took a roundabout route to avoid the heavy traffic.
He explained the bad news in a roundabout way.

definition: A flat part at the back of a boat or plane used for steering.

collocations.example: The ship's rudder was damaged badly during the violent storm.
With a broken rudder, the small boat could not steer.

definition: To search for something by moving things around untidily.

collocations.example: She began to rummage through the drawer looking for a pen.
He rummaged around in the garage for an old hammer.

definition: A boring, fixed routine that is hard to change.

collocations.example: I felt stuck in a rut doing the same job daily.
A short holiday helped her get out of a rut.

definition: A weekly day of rest and worship in some religions.

collocations.example: Many families keep the Sabbath by resting and praying together.
The shops stay closed as the town observes the Sabbath.

definition: A person who enjoys being cruel and causing others pain.

collocations.example: Only a cruel sadist would treat a helpless animal that way.
The guard acted like a sadist toward the frightened prisoners.

definition: A trip to see or hunt wild animals, usually in Africa.

collocations.example: We hope to go on safari in Kenya next summer.
The children saw real lions at the local safari park.

definition: Clean and free from dirt that could cause disease.

collocations.example: The sanitary conditions in the old camp were truly appalling.
The village still lacks basic sanitary facilities for clean water.

definition: Systems for keeping places clean, especially removing waste and dirty water.

collocations.example: Poor sanitation in the slums led to a cholera outbreak.
Proper sanitation can prevent many diseases from spreading quickly.

definition: The use of remarks that mean the opposite in order to mock or hurt.

collocations.example: There was heavy sarcasm in the way he thanked me.
She answered with a hint of sarcasm in her voice.

definition: A wide, flat area of grassland with few trees, usually in hot regions.

collocations.example: Herds of zebra roam freely across the African savannah.
Lions rest under lone trees on the open savannah.

definition: A type of shellfish with a soft body and a fan-shaped shell, eaten as food.

collocations.example: The chef served a grilled scallop on a bed of rice.
We bought fresh scallop and shrimp from the fish market.

definition: A person unfairly blamed for the mistakes or faults of others.

collocations.example: They tried to make me a scapegoat for the failed project.
The junior clerk became a scapegoat for the whole team.

definition: To search for and collect usable things among waste or remains.

collocations.example: Stray dogs scavenge for food near the back of restaurants.
The poor children scavenge through rubbish looking for scrap metal.

definition: To speak about something in a mocking way, as if it is silly.

collocations.example: Critics used to scoff at the idea of electric cars.
Don't scoff at his plan until you have really tried it.

definition: To go or move somewhere quickly.

collocations.example: Could you scoot over so I can sit down too?
I'd better scoot now or I'll miss the last train.

definition: The written text of a film, including the words and directions.

collocations.example: She spent two years trying to write her first screenplay.
The film won an award for best original screenplay.

definition: A person who copied documents by hand before printing existed.

collocations.example: A medieval scribe could spend months copying a single book.
Before printing, he worked as a scribe for the church.

definition: The loose skin or hair at the back of the neck.

collocations.example: She lifted the kitten gently by the scruff of its neck.
He grabbed the dog by the scruff and pulled it back.

definition: To run with quick, short steps, often to escape.

collocations.example: The crab tried to scuttle away across the wet sand.
Mice scuttle across the kitchen floor when the lights go off.

definition: The act of formally leaving a country or large group.

collocations.example: The southern states chose to declare secession from the union.
Most delegates refused to vote for secession from the nation.

definition: The department that handles the administrative work of a large organization.

collocations.example: The UN secretariat prepared the report for the coming meeting.
The secretariat will take several actions before the summit begins.

definition: To feel very angry but keep it hidden inside.

collocations.example: She sat quietly, but you could see her seethe with anger.
He didn't shout; he just seethed inside for hours.

definition: Very important and strongly influencing later developments.

collocations.example: The book is a seminal work in modern computer science.
Her essay became a seminal text for later researchers.

definition: A snake, especially a large one.

collocations.example: A giant serpent slid silently through the tall grass.
The statue showed a coiled serpent around a wooden staff.

definition: A soft rock formed from clay that splits easily into thin layers.

collocations.example: Oil can be extracted from shale using special methods.
The country's shale gas boom lowered energy prices sharply.

definition: A small vegetable like an onion, with a mild flavor.

collocations.example: Add some chopped shallot to the pan before the garlic.
The salad was topped with crispy fried shallot and herbs.

definition: Something that is not what it claims to be; a fake.

collocations.example: Their happy marriage turned out to be a complete sham.
The report exposed the charity as a clever sham.

definition: A person believed to heal people and contact spirits in some cultures.

collocations.example: The sick man was carried to the village shaman for healing.
The tribe would consult a shaman before any long journey.

definition: To walk slowly and awkwardly, dragging your feet.

collocations.example: The tired old man began to shamble slowly along the path.
The zombies shamble forward with stiff, dragging steps.

definition: A piece of cloth worn over the shoulders or head for warmth.

collocations.example: She wore a warm woollen shawl over her thin dress.
He wrapped a shawl around the sleeping baby's shoulders.

definition: An Arab leader, especially the head of a tribe or family.

collocations.example: The powerful sheikh owned most of the land around here.
The sheikh welcomed the visitors into his large tent.

definition: An old British coin, used until 1971.

collocations.example: The boy earned just one shilling a week back then.
She didn't have a spare shilling to buy fresh bread.

definition: The front part of the leg below the knee.

collocations.example: The player left the field with a painful shin injury.
She gave him a sharp kick on the shin.

definition: A large group of fish swimming together.

collocations.example: The shark circled slowly around the shoal of fish.
A large shoal moved as one beneath the small boat.

definition: A fast way of writing using symbols instead of full words.

collocations.example: The reporter learned to write in shorthand very quickly.
She trained as a shorthand typist after leaving school.

definition: The entertainment industry, such as film, music, and theater.

collocations.example: He threw one of the biggest showbiz parties of the year.
Life in the showbiz world can be exciting but exhausting.

definition: A final argument or contest to settle a dispute.

collocations.example: The vote pushed the leaders toward a final showdown.
The two rivals are heading for a dramatic showdown.

definition: To push or move something, especially to one side.

collocations.example: Workers shunt the old carriages onto a quiet side track.
They shunt the heavy trolley aside to clear the path.

definition: A letter of the Greek alphabet, often used as a symbol in statistics.

collocations.example: The factory uses Six Sigma methods to reduce production errors.
The sigma symbol often stands for the standard deviation.

definition: The flat shelf at the bottom of a window.

collocations.example: A small cat sat watching birds on the window sill.
She left the fresh pie to cool on the sill.

definition: Fine sand or soil carried by water and left behind.

collocations.example: The flooding river began to deposit silt across the fields.
A thick layer of silt covered the bottom of the lake.

definition: One of the air-filled spaces in the bones of the face near the nose.

collocations.example: I often suffer from headaches and sinus problems in winter.
The doctor said a sinus infection was causing the pain.

definition: To make a hissing sound, like food frying in hot oil.

collocations.example: The bacon began to sizzle in the hot frying pan.
You could hear the onions sizzle as they hit the oil.

definition: Relating to the bones of the body.

collocations.example: The long skeletal structure suggests the animal once lived in water.
Archaeologists found skeletal remains buried beneath the old church.

definition: To change results so they are not accurate or fair.

collocations.example: A few extreme answers can badly skew the survey results.
Leaving out older people would skew the data completely.

definition: A short, minor fight between small groups.

collocations.example: After a brief skirmish, the two patrols pulled back.
A border skirmish broke out between the two armies.

definition: To go around the edge of something.

collocations.example: The narrow road skirts the lake before reaching the village.
We skirted around the muddy field to stay dry.

definition: Very informal words used by a particular group of people.

collocations.example: 'Old man' is a slang term for 'father' in some families.
The teenagers spoke in street slang the adults couldn't follow.

definition: To move smoothly along the ground like a snake.

collocations.example: The snake began to slither across the warm stone path.
The baby learned to slither down from the high sofa.

definition: A small, thin piece of something.

collocations.example: A thin sliver of light showed under the closed door.
She cut only a thin sliver of the rich cake.

definition: Thick, soft, wet mud or waste.

collocations.example: The treatment plant must dispose of tons of sewage sludge.
Thick sludge had settled at the bottom of the tank.

definition: An insulting remark that damages someone's reputation.

collocations.example: She dared to cast a slur on his good character.
Using a racial slur can get an employee fired quickly.

definition: To smile in a silly or unpleasant, self-satisfied way.

collocations.example: It was hard not to smirk at his silly excuse.
She bit her lip and tried not to smirk during the meeting.

definition: To burn slowly without flames.

collocations.example: The campfire continued to smolder for hours after midnight.
Wet leaves began to smolder and produce thick gray smoke.

definition: A dirty mark made by rubbing something.

collocations.example: There was a dark smudge of ink on his forehead.
She had a smudge of chocolate on her clean shirt.

definition: A trap for catching small animals, usually with a loop.

collocations.example: The hunter set a snare along the rabbit's usual path.
I felt like an animal caught in a tight snare.

definition: To suddenly blow air out of your nose and mouth in a noisy way.

collocations.example: Dust in the old room made me sneeze loudly twice.
Please sneeze into a tissue to stop germs from spreading.

definition: To cut something with quick, small cuts using scissors.

collocations.example: She used scissors to snip off the loose thread.
He began to snip away at the edge of the paper.

definition: A form of tobacco in powder that is breathed in through the nose.

collocations.example: The old man took a pinch of snuff from his tin.
In those days many gentlemen liked to take snuff.

definition: To make something dirty.

collocations.example: Be careful not to soil your clothes with wet paint.
The muddy dog will soil the clean carpet again.

definition: The bottom part of a foot or shoe.

collocations.example: The hot sand burned the soles of their bare feet.
These boots have a thick rubber sole for better grip.

definition: A poem with fourteen lines and a fixed rhyme pattern.

collocations.example: Shakespeare could write a sonnet about love and time.
The composer chose to set a sonnet to gentle music.

definition: Black powder produced when something burns.

collocations.example: Their faces were covered in soot after the fire.
A thick layer of soot coated the old chimney walls.

definition: A singer with the highest female or boy's singing voice.

collocations.example: The lead soprano received a long round of applause.
She has a clear soprano voice of fine quality.

definition: A person who is believed to use magic powers.

collocations.example: The evil sorcerer cast a spell over the whole village.
A powerful sorcerer guarded the tower with dark magic.

definition: A bean used to make foods like sauce, milk, and oil.

collocations.example: I like my fried eggs with a little soy sauce.
She drinks soy milk instead of ordinary cow's milk.

definition: To practice boxing with light blows.

collocations.example: He stepped into the ring to spar with an old friend.
The young boxer will spar a few rounds before lunch.

definition: A sudden, uncontrolled tightening of a muscle.

collocations.example: A sudden muscle spasm made her drop the heavy box.
The injection sent his tired leg into a spasm.

definition: A large number of similar things happening close together.

collocations.example: The city has seen a spate of car thefts lately.
The bombing was the latest in a spate of attacks.

definition: A very small spot or piece of something.

collocations.example: There wasn't a speck of dust anywhere in the room.
The ship was now just a tiny speck on the horizon.

definition: The band of colors seen when light passes through a prism.

collocations.example: A rainbow shows the full visible spectrum of sunlight.
Each color in the spectrum has a different wavelength.

definition: A tall, pointed structure on top of a church or tower.

collocations.example: You can see the church spire from across the valley.
The cathedral's pointed spire rose high above the town.

definition: A tiny cell by which some plants and fungi reproduce.

collocations.example: Each tiny fungal spore can grow into a new plant.
The mushrooms release spores into the damp evening air.

definition: A tube or lip through which liquid pours out.

collocations.example: She tilted the kettle spout carefully over the small cup.
Water dripped slowly from the cracked teapot spout.

definition: A short period of doing a lot of one enjoyable activity.

collocations.example: She went on a shopping spree after her first paycheck.
People went on a spending spree before the new tax.

definition: A small stem with leaves or flowers.

collocations.example: I decorated the fruit salad with a fresh sprig of mint.
Add a small sprig of parsley on top of the dish.

definition: A tall evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves.

collocations.example: A tall spruce tree stood at the edge of the garden.
They hiked for hours through the dark spruce forest.

definition: To flow out suddenly in a strong stream.

collocations.example: Flames began to spurt out from the burning roof.
Blood can spurt from a deep cut very quickly.

definition: To argue noisily about something unimportant.

collocations.example: The children squabble over the last piece of cake.
The couple squabble about money almost every single day.

definition: To waste money, time, or chances carelessly.

collocations.example: He didn't squander his money on flashy cars or clothes.
Don't squander this rare chance to study abroad.

definition: A sea animal with a long soft body and ten arms.

collocations.example: A giant squid can grow longer than a city bus.
We ordered grilled squid with lemon at the seaside café.

definition: A man who owned most of the land in a country area.

collocations.example: The local squire owned nearly every farm in the valley.
The village squire invited the whole parish to his estate.

definition: To make liquid shoot out in a thin, fast stream.

collocations.example: The children love to squirt water at each other outside.
Just squirt a little oil onto the squeaky door hinge.

definition: (Of water) not flowing and often stale or dirty.

collocations.example: Mosquitoes breed quickly in the warm, stagnant water nearby.
The old stagnant pond was covered with green slime.
